title: Why Your Recorded Voice Sounds Wrong
caption:
That squeaky stranger on your phone is you
He records a voice note, plays it back, and freezes: the voice sounds thin, high and nothing like his own. Then a skull diagram explains why.
When you speak, you hear yourself two ways: sound through the air, plus vibrations your skull carries straight to the inner ear, which adds low-frequency bass. A recording captures only the air version, so playback sounds higher and thinner. Bone conduction is the missing bass filter.
When did you last hear your own recorded voice and not recognise it?
Save this for the next time a voice note shocks you
